text:
Sandis Vilmanis was a fifth-round pick, a Latvian who went through Lulea, the OHL and the AHL before getting here, and he's making it hard for Florida to send him back. Florida Hockey Now's headline: "Sandis Vilmanis Playing Like an NHL Regular, Deserves to Stay with Panthers."

He has 4 goals and 10 points in 22 games on 12:44 a night, with 8 points in his last ten, including a game-winning goal against Buffalo on Nov. 21. Our numbers call the hot stretch partly real: the chances are up a little, but finishing is doing most of the work. He hits (64 of them) and the Panthers win 56.1% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him, almost seven points better than without him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from a small sample, says his offense lives in transition, with 55% of his shots off the rush. His closest matches are depth grinders like Nick Cousins and Elmer Soderblom, which is the job: limited minutes, heavy hits, keep chances down. On a team that values that role as much as Florida does, it's a real way to stick.
headline: Vilmanis is forcing his way in
